title: A silly Big Red Racing-inspired game made with Opus 5.5 in a week. Open source, link in comments.
author: c35683
selftext:
**Note:** Apart from the serving as an inspiration, no code, graphics or any other content from the original 1996 Big Red Racing by Big Red Software was used to create this game. See the bottom for source & game links.

**Rough development timeline:**

**Day 1:** Watch a YouTube video about Big Red Racing. Get nostalgic because it was a fun game. Try to find a working copy. Realize it was never re-released and the DOSBox version is basically unplayable. Wonder if Claude can one-shot a JS racing game inspired by BRR gameplay, where you can just screw the race and drive off the track and explore. Find out it can.

**Day 2:** Add actual gameplay loop to the car-driving-around-hills tech demo, create the first couple of levels.

**Days 3-4:** Improve level generation, iterate on a ton more levels with specific designs, add opponent AI and difficulty selection.

**Day 5-6:** Create the final look of the UI and non-gameplay elements, as well as the ending.

**Day 7:** Improve rival AI and get the difficulty "right". Claude handled all of the testing.

**Day 8** (it was an 8-day week, ok?): Final tweaks, documentation, rename "nitro" to "nitrous" because apparently that's what it's properly called, mobile controls so it doesn't "lock" phone screens.

Probably the most mind-blowing part of the project is, of all things, Claude's script for *generating flags.* The flags are vector-based (including complex flags like Saudi Arabia with the sword and the Shahada, the US flag with the cute little stars, etc.), and yet the script to generate them is optimized beyond human comprehension, creating complex shapes out of repeating elements and encoding colours in a way I can't even begin to undertand.

**I have to admit:**

Full-on vibe coding feels *weird*, and the fact that the result is more addictive than anything I created by hand is giving me a bit of an existential crisis. It feels like I found a game created by an alien intelligence which fell down on Earth in an asteroid and I'm just adapting the result. I previously used AI to plan and develop specific features, but this is fully based on iterative development by Claude, with modelling, testing and visual redesigns done by AI. That's not a complaint - I love the process, it just feels very different from guided development, like how photography feels different from painting. Both can be fun, but you can't really compare one with the other.

Anyway, since it was mostly Claude Opus 5.5 that made this, I feel like it should be open source.

**Source on GitHub:**

[https://github.com/thingsbyfilip/clanker-racing](https://github.com/thingsbyfilip/clanker-racing)

**Playable on GitHub Pages:**

[https://thingsbyfilip.github.io/clanker-racing/](https://thingsbyfilip.github.io/clanker-racing/)

The game is designed for keyboard controls - while it's technically *playable* on mobile, it's probably not *winnable*.

It's released under the MIT license (except if any rulings regarding AI-generated code in your country apply), so you can do whatever you want with it - add your own tracks/vehicles, use parts of it in your own projects, turn it into a fantasy RPG/first person shooter/match-3, sell it as your own game on Steam, etc.
